sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.4% a year from $38.5 billion in FY2016 to $67.6 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was cyclical rather than steady: revenue rose 18.0% in FY2017 and 20.4% in FY2018, fell 22.4% in FY2020, then climbed 22.1% in FY2021 and 12.8% in FY2023 [D42][D92][D198][D251][D357].
The FY2020 drop came from lower sales volume driven by lower end-user demand and dealer inventory reductions across all three primary segments [P59].
The FY2023 peak reflected favorable price realization and higher sales volume, with dealer inventory up about $2.1 billion during the year [P32].
North America supplied the growth: its share of revenue rose from 46.8% in FY2018 to 54.2% in FY2025, contributing 3.4pp of the 4.3% revenue growth in FY2025 [D494][D513][D515][D463].
FY2025 sales rose on higher sales volume of $3.389 billion, partly offset by unfavorable price realization of $817 million [P13].
Power & Energy did the heavy lifting, growing 11.6% and contributing 5.2pp, while Construction Industries fell 1.6% and subtracted 0.6pp [D758][D759][D765][D766].
Construction Industries' decline came from unfavorable price realization of $1.136 billion, partly offset by higher sales volume of $568 million [P8].
Operating costs grew 4.8pp faster than revenue in FY2025, at 9.1%, and incremental operating margin was -69.1% [D489][D481][D488].
Operating margin of 16.5% in FY2025 sat above the 14.3% window median but below the 20.2% FY2024 high and well above the 3.0% FY2016 low [F30][D1123][D1122][D1121].
The 3.7pp margin decline in FY2025 was driven by unfavorable manufacturing costs of $2.148 billion, largely tariffs, and unfavorable price realization of $817 million [D476][P9].
Cost of revenue accounted for -4.2pp of the FY2025 bridge, while R&D added 0.1pp and SG&A was flat [D490][D491][D492].
In FY2025 net margin of 13.1% sat 3.4pp below the 16.5% operating margin, with a 24.0% effective tax rate [F50][F30][D1168][D449].
Operating cash flow of $11.7 billion was 1.32x net income in FY2025, above the 1.16x window median, and free cash flow covered net income at 1.00x [F80][F40][D450][D1158][D451].
Machinery, Power & Energy operating cash flow rose to $12.278 billion from $11.437 billion on lower working capital requirements and lower cash taxes paid [P4].

Free cash flow margin of 13.2% was below the 16.8% FY2023 high and above the 11.9% median, as capex rose 41.9% to $2.821 billion, 4.2% of revenue and 1.25x D&A [D447][D1128][D1129][D470][F90][D446][D452].
The investing outflow widened because of lower securities maturities, more intercompany lending to Financial Products and higher capital expenditures [P3].
Net debt was $26.2 billion at FY2025, with cash of $9.980 billion and total debt of $36.210 billion [D456][F140][D455].

That net-cash ratio ranked at the 67th percentile of three industrials peers against a -59.4% median, though the pack omits long-term debt due within one year, $7.1 billion in FY2025 [D1169][D1170][R7].
Buybacks of $5.190 billion plus dividends of $2.749 billion were 89.0% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 3.5% [X140][X150][D459][D483].
Return on average equity of 43.5% topped the 23.3% peer median, but leverage is understated by the missing current maturities [D462][D1156][R7].
Long-term debt due within one year, $7.1 billion in FY2025, sits in no line of the pack, so total debt and net cash omit it across FY2016-FY2025 [R7][X180][D455].
The omission understates leverage and makes the peer net-cash comparison unreliable [R7].
Net debt rose for a second year in FY2025, from $22.1 billion in FY2023 to $24.9 billion in FY2024 and $26.2 billion in FY2025 [R1][D350][D403][D456].
Rising debt alongside a 14.7% operating-income decline is the balance-sheet pressure to watch [R1][D464].
Net income for FY2021-FY2025 in the table comes from the proxy's pay-versus-performance table, not the 10-K, differing by up to 0.06% [R3][F40][X20].
The gap is immaterial to margins but matters where precision is claimed [R3].
Whether FY2026 operating margin holds above the 14.3% window median or falls toward the 3.0% low, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D1123][D1121].
Whether capex stays above 4.2% of revenue or falls back toward the 2.9% FY2016 level, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D446][D6].
Whether net debt moves back below the $22.1 billion FY2023 level or extends past $26.2 billion, reported in the FY2026 10-K [D350][D456].
